\begin{example} \end{example}[Orthogonal bisectional curvature preserves Ricci curvature] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0226 1. ch13:13.7\group Kahler Curvature Conditions

If a Kähler--Ricci flow starts with nonnegative Ricci curvature and positive orthogonal bisectional curvature is preserved, then Ricci curvature remains nonnegative. \end{example}
Proof

\sketch At a first zero of the least Ricci eigenvalue, its reaction term is a sum of orthogonal bisectional curvatures weighted by nonnegative Ricci eigenvalues. It and the Laplacian term are nonnegative, so the maximum principle excludes passage into negative Ricci curvature.

□
